applies_to: the raw bytes of JCS(statement), the bytes the content-address is computed over

derivation.max_statement_bytes: 2 * 2592 + 1024 = 6208. 2592 bytes is the largest public key among the families this profile admits (ML-DSA-87, FIPS 204; ML-DSA-44/65 are 1312/1952 bytes, every SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) parameter set is at most 64), carried as hex in pq_pubkey, so 5184 bytes. 1024 bytes covers every other member: the largest non-key overhead among the published statements is 313 bytes (the SLH-DSA rotation statement), so 1024 is chosen headroom, not a measured maximum.
derivation.max_member_name_escaped_bytes: 64 escaped bytes per member name. The longest published member name is 27 bytes (predecessor_content_address). The bound is what makes the member-ordering rule decidable from a fixed window, which an on-chain segment fraud proof needs. max_member_name_escaped_bytes MUST be strictly less than the fraud-proof segment size; the one-segment refutation depends on it. This profile's 64 is under the 256-byte segment the published PinpointJcsAnchor deployment uses.

admission: Checked in this order; the first failing check gives the verdict. (1) Size: JCS(statement) is at most max_statement_bytes, checked on the raw byte length before parsing (reject:size_exceeded). (2) Shape: a JSON object whose member values are strings, integers, or objects whose member values are strings or integers, one level of nesting (reject:unsupported_shape). (3) Canonical form: the raw bytes are exactly JCS(statement) and every integer is within +-(2^53 - 1) (reject:not_canonical). (4) Member names, nested ones included, are at most max_member_name_escaped_bytes in escaped form (reject:name_too_long). A statement failing any check MUST NOT be resolved as a binding. On chain, (1) is enforceable at admission from the raw length alone; (2)-(4) can be settled by a bounded fraud proof within a challenge window, inheriting its one-honest-watcher assumption (informative).
governs: Selected by the consumer's configured enforcement profile, not by anything in the statement: a consumer enforcing pq_key_binding.v1 applies this facet to every binding statement it admits. A statement's own profile member is a deployment label and is not read (D3). The published v0 statements, including the per-agent statements with a nested subject, are admitted unchanged and are in the vector corpus as admit cases.
scope: Canonical form only. This facet does not change the cutoff rule, the content-address, or in-force resolution.
versioning: Per profile and versioned. A profile that admits a family with a larger public key declares its own facet with the same derivation; it never amends this one. A later profile MUST keep max_member_name_escaped_bytes strictly less than its fraud-proof segment size. Raising the name bound to or above that size drops the one-segment refutation, and re-deriving the size bound does not catch it.
